newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Diesel edges up on crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Diesel edges up on crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged up at midday on Monday on firmer crude prices with market fundamentals seen unchanged as players looked to fresh demand from China to boost the market, traders said.
"The market is going nowhere at the moment but sentiment is better because most people think China will come back to buy," one trader said.
July gasoil swaps were last quoted at $22.50/$22.60 per barrel, August at $22.90/$23.10, both up 10 cents from Friday on quiet trade, brokers said.
August Brent crude futures in London rose 33 cents to settle at $18.18 per barrel.
Traders said the market is holding its own despite the sporadic cut-throat offers that are made by some players seeking to either get rid of surplus barrels quickly or to bring down spot prices.
Over the last week two cargoes traded well below prevailing spot prices, one on Tuesday at $21.50 and the other on Friday at $21.70, both on a free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis.
The physical prices were at about 50-70 cents below the next best offers prevailing at that time and were also priced at similar discounts to the swaps market.

Traders said the equivalent discount of up to 70 cents to the swaps market for prompt physical cargoes were not reflecting the discount of about 20 cents that are achieved for barrels lifting at those forwards of mid-July.
These offers as a result have also attracted a slew of buyers with the seller only having one cargo to sell each time, traders said.
Aside from these occasional cheap offers, the market has held steady at above the $22.00-mark with an upside seen from the expected demand from China, Indonesia and India for August delivery cargoes.
The jet/gas oil spreads were steady with July regrade quoted at $2.00/$2.20.
Fuel oil swaps were unchanged after the hectic physical trading on Friday where two 380-cst cargoes traded at $95.50 per tonne and one 180-cst cargo done at $100.00.
July swaps was last quoted steady at $99.25/$100.00 per tonne.
